rationale: Two ontology types this lane had no verdict for, pinned together because they are the same claim seen from two sides: what a Sass module OFFERS, and what one binding REPLACES. A `.scss` file IS a Sass module — `@use './theme'` loads any stylesheet and exposes its top-level variables, mixins and functions — so a module's public surface is a graph fact and not a naming convention, and the edges are what make `@use 'a', 'b'` answerable. `exports` is therefore pinned with its BOTH-ends-resolve property: the source is the file's own module symbol and the target is a symbol the file publishes, so no edge names a member of another file. Sass's PRIVATE-MEMBER rule is pinned as a FORBIDDEN row because it is the only thing stopping the table from being 'every top-level symbol': `-`/`_` marks a member private to its module and `@use` does not expose it, so an export edge to one would claim a contract the language does not offer. `$local` is the second forbidden row and it is the SCOPE half of the same rule: an assignment inside a rule body is a local, not a member. `overrides` is pinned at its narrowest honest width, and the two exclusions beside it are the measurement: a `!default` on an already-assigned name is SKIPPED by Sass rather than applied (`$brand: #0f0 !default` after `$brand: #f00`), so it replaces nothing and gets no edge; a `!global` assignment of a name the file never assigned at the top level CREATES a global rather than replacing one, so `$invented` gets no edge either. Those two `forbidRelationships` rows are what stop a later widening of this class from being free. The `overridesLine` pin is the same provenance discipline the `line_number` pins carry: an override whose prior declaration line is dropped connects two versions of one binding with nothing to tell them apart.
